1.explanation: To implement the new flushAlignment prop, the main Accordion component needs to accept and forward a boolean flushAlignment prop, apply a modifier class (e.g. `${prefix}--accordion--flushAlignment`) in its className builder, and declare it in propTypes. The AccordionItem component must also pick up that prop (directly or via context/…rest) and add a corresponding modifier on its heading and content containers so that CSS can remove the padding. Both the Accordion class (for prop definition and top-level styling) and the AccordionItem class (for per-item layout adjustments) are the key loci for this change.
1.bug_scenario: The design calls for a new “flush alignment” mode on the Accordion component where both the heading text and the expanded body content sit flush against the left divider line, eliminating the default left padding. The screenshots illustrate closed and open accordion items with their text and content flush to the divider lines rather than indented.

2.explanation:
1. Accordion.js::Accordion – this is the root component that must accept the new flushAlignment prop, add a modifier class (e.g. `${prefix}--accordion--flush`) to the container, and forward the prop via `...rest` or explicitly to its items.  
2. AccordionItem.js::AccordionItem – each item renders the heading (`<Toggle>` with `${prefix}--accordion__heading`) and content (`${prefix}--accordion__content`). These classes need to include conditional styles when flushAlignment is true (removing default left padding).  
3. Accordion.stories.js::Playground – the story for the component must expose the new prop in the controls (`argTypes`) and demonstrate the flush alignment variant.  
4. Accordion-test.js::describe('Accordion') – tests should be updated to cover the flushAlignment prop for both rendering (snapshot or DOM assertions) and accessibility (no a11y violations with the new alignment).  
All of these modules handle the API surface, rendering, and verification of the Accordion component, so they must be updated to fully support and test the new flushAlignment feature.
2.bug_scenario: The design requires a new “flushAlignment” prop on the Accordion so that both the heading text and panel body sit flush against the left divider lines (no extra left padding). In the closed state, each title should line up exactly at the divider. In the open state, both the title and the expanded content should also align flush to that same divider.
